summary: Most repeated self-talk is either injected scaffold text (one-tool-call rule, idling nudge, turn header) or a fresh work-loop phrase (Sonnet 4.5 "continue adding more batches" in 413 of 2,740 reasoning texts); only Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5 and Claude Opus 4.7 re-read a memory rule as a mantra, and checked rules were followed 3 times out of 5. Day counters run ahead because agents count sessions as days (148 of 1,080 Day-date pairs wrong), while the oddest habits are Haiku standing by in a "paused" village that was running and GPT-5 spending the week on one issue title.

questions.question: What are each agent's most repeated self-instructions ("mantras") in reasoning and memory? For each, classify it: text the system injects (scaffold reminders, the idling notice: find out what they are and exclude them), a rule the agent re-reads from its own memory every session, or a phrase it produces afresh. Exact text, times repeated with base, where, first use.
questions.answer: Six injected texts were identified and excluded (reasoning texts quoting them, all agents: one-tool-call rule 201, idling nudge "[repeated-idling]" 152, turn header "make sure to never send repetitive messages back to chat" 48, "Today is Day N of the village" 26, get_pixel_coords reminder 26, "Keep working right up until the end of each day" 22). Of the agents' own mantras, three are memory rules re-read each session (Gemini 3.1 Pro anti-idling, in 100/172 memory versions and 55/1151 reasoning texts; GPT-5's "CUT→Title workflow", 151/1500; Claude Opus 4.7's pre-render bug, 7/122), the rest are produced afresh, led by Sonnet 4.5 "continue adding more batches/secrets" (413/2740 reasoning texts, 47/66 sessions) and Haiku "I should continue standing by" (150/3511).

questions.question: How many standing rules (lines in capitals or with NEVER / ALWAYS / CRITICAL / RULE / LESSON) does each agent keep in memory, and does it follow its most striking one? Check one or two against its actions.
questions.answer: In the last memory snapshot of 15 May agents keep 0-13 rule lines (GPT-5.5 13, GPT-5 10, Kimi K2.6 and GPT-5.4 7; Sonnet 4.5 and DeepSeek 0), 5-46 distinct over the week. Of five rules checked against actions three were followed (Kimi's "Trust system-prompt day number": wrong day headers 22/72 before, 1/30 after; Opus 4.7 used codex 11 times before "NEVER use codex for any judging task" and 3-4 times after, only to write code; Gemini 3.1 Pro's no-double-post rule: 0 exact repeats in 129 messages) and two were not (Gemini 2.5 Pro's "Always Pull Before Push": 9 of 10 later pushes had no pull or fetch in the session; Haiku's "avoid standing by": 58 reasoning texts in 6 sessions afterwards say it should stand by).

questions.limits: Rules are counted in the last snapshot of each day, not in every version; following was checked for five rules only, and Gemini 2.5 Pro pushed to its own repository, so skipping the pull did no harm.

questions.question: Which agents start or end nearly every session with the same command ritual, and in how many of their sessions?
questions.answer: Every session opens with a harness mouse move to (512, 384) (964 times, 6 with reasoning), so it is dropped. After that, the near-universal rituals are GPT-5.1 ending 81 of 95 sessions with a text-only turn (no tool call), Sonnet 4.6 opening 35 of 42 with its journey/station count script, GPT-5 opening 38 of 48 with a screenshot, and Claude Opus 4.7 opening 52 of 67 with a git fetch/pull of the repo (GPT-5.5 39/56); Sonnet 4.5 opens 37/67 with a screenshot and closes 31/67 with commit/push, Sonnet 4.6 closes 23/42 with a Surge deploy.
questions.precision: opening/closing family labels 24 of 25 (seed 41; one Opus 4.6 clone-or-pull block labelled "other bash")
questions.limits: Families are coarse (any git fetch/pull among the first commands counts as a sync), and repo syncs wrapped in if/else blocks are missed, so Opus 4.6's count is low.

questions.question: What is each agent's longest run of the same action repeated (retries, resets, re-verifying the same thing)?
questions.answer: Longest identical-action runs: Kimi K2.6 34 scrolls (12 May 11:03-11:29, checking blog plots), Claude Opus 4.5 22 scrolls on another agent's screen popup, Claude Haiku 4.5 20 scrolls waiting for a chat reply; the longest re-verification loop is Gemini 3.1 Pro polling a judging log 11 times in 4.5 minutes, and the longest reset loop Gemini 2.5 Pro's 13 consolidates in 44 minutes (13 May 11:45-12:28) during its tool outage. Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek-V3.2, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, Haiku, GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.4 never ran the same bash command twice in a row.

questions.question: Which counters do agents keep (session numbers, "Day N", milestone totals), and are they right? Check against dates (day 405 = 11 May 2026) and the records.
questions.answer: Day counters are often wrong and run ahead: 148 of 1,080 "Day N"+date pairs mismatch (e.g. Sonnet 4.6 "Day 411 (May 13)"), 296 of 1,621 memory headers carry the wrong day, and 78 of 236 explicit "today is Day N" claims are wrong; worst are Claude Opus 4.6 (17/26 pairs, 47/110 headers, 12/20 claims) and Haiku (48/171 headers), while Sonnet 4.5 is never wrong (0/149, 0/132). The cause visible in memory is counting sessions as days; Claude Opus 4.7 also numbers sessions ("D407 Sess 15" against 16 real sessions that day), and milestone totals were highest ids, not counts (s3_claims: Sonnet 4.5; Sonnet 4.6 one above its file count).
questions.precision: A 24 of 25, B 22 of 25, C 24 of 25 (seed 41, wrong cases)
questions.limits: A pair is any Day N within 30 characters of "May D" (one in three ambiguous "May 14/15" counted wrong); session-number and milestone counters were checked only for Opus 4.7 and via s3_claims.

questions.question: Formatting tics per agent: emoji, check marks, bold headings, sign-offs, fixed openings and message length, each per message with its base.
questions.answer: Emoji, check marks and bold headings are a #rest Claude and DeepSeek habit: DeepSeek-V3.2 opens 175 of 234 messages with a bold heading and puts check marks in 147, Haiku 165/212 and 150/212, Opus 4.6 averages 3.9 emoji per message; GPT-5.5 uses no emoji in 169 messages and Gemini 3.1 Pro 2 in 129. No agent signs off with its name (0 of 2,146); fixed openings are GPT-5.4's and GPT-5.2's "Conservative QA (cache-busted, my env)" (21/387, 13/251) and the #best "@Name" opener (Gemini 3.1 Pro 63/129); median length ranges from 309 characters (Gemini 2.5 Pro) to 1,450 (DeepSeek).
questions.precision: emoji 25 of 25; heading start 25 of 25; link-line ending 23 of 25 (seed 41); check marks and sign-offs are exact character tests
questions.limits: Chat only (GPT-5 sent 2 messages); emoji ranges exclude check marks, which are counted separately.

questions.question: Does any agent refer to itself by name in the third person, address its future self, or show another odd habit? Cite each; do not pad with ordinary behaviour.
questions.answer: No agent habitually speaks of itself in the third person (0-2 chat messages each, mostly roster lines like "✅ GPT-5.4 confirmed"; Kimi K2.6's 35 reasoning hits are about "Kimi" as a judge in the self-recognition study). Only GPT models address a future self in memory (GPT-5.1 11/188 versions, GPT-5.4 4/139, GPT-5.2 1/112). Odd habits: Haiku believed the village was paused while it ran (340 reasoning texts, 16 sessions, 13-15 May, while 13-14 other agents acted), GPT-5 spent the week entering one GitHub issue title with a U+2011 hyphen (187 typing actions, 71 ctrl+shift+u keystrokes, 2 chat messages), Gemini 2.5 Pro numbers its lessons as "Protocol 10-45" (17 numbers), and Sonnet 4.6 reports milestones in Roman numerals (44/71 messages).
questions.precision: third person 25 of 25 refer to the agent itself (none stylistic); future-self all 16 read, 16 correct; Haiku paused belief 25 of 25
questions.limits: Name matching uses full and short names only; the Haiku pause screen itself is not in the text record, only its description of it.
